# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

- **External editor** — init default `nvim` (independent of `enableVimMode`); `editorcfg status/list/use/reset/doctor` manages the local override. `EDITOR`/`VISUAL` name `dotfiles-editor`, which resolves and waits on each invocation. Micro is baseline devtools; code/cursor presets add `--wait`. See `docs/tools/editor.md`. Local `editor-choice` is not chezmoi-managed.

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, Pi (`pi`), Oh My Pi (`omp`), the `pia` Git-managed harness-combo manager, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). `pia doctor` checks the stack; `pia list --tree` / `pia use pi/base` select presets. The external checkout is `~/.local/share/pi-agents`; `08_pi_agents.sh` makes its canonical commands beat mise/Bun shadows, while runtime state and credentials stay elsewhere. Token-usage tracking: `tokens` (tokens.ci; binary only — `tokens login` / `tokens serve` are manual opt-ins, see `docs/tools/tokens.md`). See `docs/tools/pi-agents.md`, `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Sidecar + `td` + Tasks** — `coding_agents` installs all three under `installCodingAgents`. Sidecar offers a companion dashboard or integrated workspace; `td` tracks agent issues; Tasks handles personal planning through `tasks` / `tasks-tui` / `tasks-api`. Tasks first-seeds user-owned XDG config/data paths; it preserves existing configuration and does not start its API. Herdr `prefix+S` opens a right companion pane, keeping the existing agent external. See `docs/tools/td_sidecar.md` (`#ux-evolution`) and `docs/tools/tasks.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **summarize** — `summarize <url|file>` turns a YouTube video, podcast, webpage, PDF or local media into a summary. Output defaults to 繁體中文 via the managed `~/.summarize/config.json` overlay. Wrappers in `32_summarize.sh`: `ytsum` (video, with timestamps), `sumq` (30-second triage), `suml` (long), `sumj` (JSON). `--cli claude|codex|gemini` reuses an already-authenticated agent instead of an API key. See `docs/tools/summarize.md`.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **mole** (`mo`, macOS only) — `mo purge` reclaims dev build artifacts (`node_modules`, `target`, `.venv`) across the roots listed in `~/.config/mole/purge_paths`; `mo analyze` is a disk explorer, `mo clean` clears caches (always `--dry-run` first, or use the `moclean` wrapper). Helpers in `33_mole.sh`: `moa`, `moclean`, `mowl`. Both config files are chezmoi `create_` seeds, and the whitelist **replaces** rather than extends mole's built-in defaults. See `docs/tools/mole.md`.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared (expose localhost to the **public** internet).
- **Tailscale** — WireGuard mesh VPN (tailnet-only, the opposite of the tunnel tools). Helper CLI: `tsnet`. Picker: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`, `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`.
- **Input method** — McBopomofo + RIME (Traditional Chinese).
- **Agent sounds** — audio notifications on agent Stop/Notification hooks. See `docs/tools/agent-sounds.md`.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Agent browser tools

**Ghostty** is GUI-managed: macOS `installBrewApps` cask; Linux desktop native
apt/PPA with classic Snap fallback (sudo, x64/arm64). Config is shared with
cmux, uses Hack Nerd Font Mono 14, padding 10, native keyboard protocols and SSH
terminfo helpers. Server hosts use a local GUI client over SSH. Details:
`docs/tools/ghostty.md`.

**Agent browser tools** have independent `installTerminalBrowser` (this host: true) and `installPlaywrightCli` (true) switches on supported macOS/Linux hosts, including servers. Use `terminal-browser open URL --split right` for a visible
shared page (Ghostty/Kitty graphics required), and
`playwright-cli -s=TASK open URL --browser=chromium` for independent headless testing. Both have package-matched
skills. Chromium preload/cache repair is opt-in (`preloadPlaywrightChromium`, this host: true). Otherwise first run `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` (Linux missing libraries: add `--with-deps`). Remote preview:
run `terminal-browser open --ssh HOST http://localhost:PORT` **locally**; a remote
agent does not automatically control that local browser. See
`docs/tools/browser-tools.md` for platform/noRoot limits and upgrades. Use the
project's own Playwright Test for committed CI tests.

## Package-managed personal CLIs

`installPersonalTools` groups dev, translate, exp and ten lazy CLIs. Full
bundles default on; cloud-vm/minimal off. Missing keys preserve legacy selection;
choose explicitly with `dotcfg --set installPersonalTools=true --yes --no-apply`.
Apply installs CLIs only (no daemons/credentials or first-use shims). New macOS
binary installs use the personal tap; Linux amd64/arm64 uses verified releases without
Go. `just upgrade-personal` preserves the active owner and skips missing/unknown
binaries; generated Bash/Zsh completions follow successful changes. See
`docs/tools/personal-tools.md`. `gopls` stays in generic `go_tools`.

- **`dev`** — repository/task/worktree command center with a TUI, parent-shell navigation, generated completion, agent-safe prepare/finalize/done/retire lifecycle, and receipt-backed `dev git` transactions. macOS installs `daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli`; Linux uses the personal release installer (legacy Go remains supported). Source: `github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli`.
- **`translate`** — terminal translator (CLI + TUI). macOS installs `daviddwlee84/tap/translate`; Linux uses the personal release installer (legacy Go remains supported).
- **`lazyclash`** — CLI/TUI for local or SSH-accessible Mihomo cores, source-backed node/group editing and explicit native/Docker client setup. macOS uses the personal tap; Linux new installs use verified releases in `~/.local/bin`, while legacy hosts retain source ownership. Upgrade through `just upgrade-personal` or the owning package manager. The apply-time completion generator owns zsh/bash files; narrow refresh: `scripts/generate_completions.sh --tool lazyclash --force`. v0.1.6+ supplies standalone `proxy shell-init` used by `50_networking.sh`: proxy-on/off own per-shell SSH sessions and restore previous env; set `LAZYCLASH_PROXY_SHELL=0` for legacy helpers. v0.1.7 adds `proxy ssh HOST [-- COMMAND...]` and foreground `proxy tunnel share HOST` for the opposite direction; printed exports belong on the remote host. Copilot startup and `docker-net on` check service lifetime and refuse known temporary SSH endpoints before side effects. Docker render/test generates consumer settings without writing the chezmoi-owned client `proxies.default`; legacy cache consumers reject private proxy credentials. Dotfiles apply installs only the CLI; `lazyclash setup` separately previews and installs a core with its own owner/rollback record. Source: `github.com/daviddwlee84/lazyclash`.

- **`exp`** — Git-based research records, execution and a read-only overview.
- **`lazychezmoi`** — inspect/edit/apply dotfile state through chezmoi.
- **`lazymlflow`** — experiment/run/artifact exploration; local stores may need MLflow separately.
- **`lazypueue`** — task and queue dashboard; Pueue daemons are configured separately.
- **`lazymermaid`** — Mermaid workbench; Neovim/termaid/Node runtime setup remains explicit.
- **`lazyset`** — local/SSH TUI catalog and retained child sessions; underlying tools install independently.
- **`lazyansible`** — personal Ansible workspace fork; existing Ansible runtime stays separately owned.
- **`lazycrontab`** — local/SSH cron inspection, readable schedules and reviewed edits; no scheduler setup during apply.
- **`lazyfind`** — local/SSH file/text search using fd/rg, with optional rga/zoxide.
- **`lazypkg`** — software inventory and reviewed package operations; mpm setup is explicit. Its `upgrade` command updates a selected package, not lazypkg itself; use `lazypkg self upgrade` for verified Homebrew ownership or `just upgrade-personal` for this CLI.

## Copilot agent launchers

`claude-copilot-once` / `codex-copilot-once` (and the identical names without
`-once`) auto-start the local proxy and inject single-session CLI settings.
`--specstory-mode run|exit|off` defaults to live recording; `exit` exports saved
history after the agent exits and retries pending sync next launch. Wrapper
flags precede agent arguments. Claude merges the effective user `--settings`
JSON/file into one CLI object; no temporary project pin. `copilot-here on`
explicitly pins Claude, previews changed settings (default keep; `--yes` for
scripts), and refuses tracked targets. `off` restores owned settings while
preserving later edits. Codex 0.156.1 ignores project-local provider settings;
use its single-session launcher. `copilot-run` remains a generic environment
injector. See `docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md`.

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
- **`agent-warmup`** — Tyro CLI that drives a real interactive Claude TUI at a scheduled time through an existing Herdr session (preferred) or tmux, with uv-first daemon bootstrap and safe fallback. See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
- **`raid-perm-check`** — read-only auditor for a group+ACL-shared data mount (`summary`/`orphans`/`groups`/`units`/`user`/`all`, default `/mnt/raid`). Catches the two silent breakages: orphaned uid/gid after an account is deleted, and a stale `systemd --user` manager whose frozen groups make timers hit EACCES on paths your shell reads fine. Never modifies — prints the fix. See `docs/sysadmin/shared-storage-permissions.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`ytmv`** — download YouTube music videos for **old MP3 players**: mp3 + sidecar `.lrc` + ID3v2.3/USLT lyrics, or mp4 with soft/burned-in subtitles. Subcommands `get` / `lyrics` / `tag` / `doctor`; `ytmv help` is the complete setup/cookie-safety guide and `doctor --cookies` explicitly tests a configured source. Public downloads use packaged EJS + managed Node 22+ cookie-free first (doctor flags legacy Node 20/16). Compatibility profiles (`safe`, `cjk-big5`, `cjk-gbk`, `ipod`, `modern`) are re-appliable offline via `ytmv tag`. Needs ffmpeg (`installMediaTools`); `--burn-subs` needs the keg-only `ffmpeg-full`. No `tv` channel by design. See `docs/tools/ytmv.md`.
- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
- **`herdr-grep`** — search visible or retained content across panes in the current, one named, or all running local Herdr sessions; reports exact session/workspace/tab/pane coordinates, supports `--json`, and `--pick` pipes matches to fzf then exact-focuses/attaches the selection. Inside Herdr, `prefix+Alt+F` opens a visible-content picker (Alt+S = scrollback, Alt+V = visible). Remote use runs the CLI through SSH. See `docs/tools/herdr.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`dev-projects`** — on-demand local REPOS candidates from `dev repo list --json`; `open PATH --tool sidecar|nvim` revalidates before launch, and `sidecar-import` previews add-only registration (`--apply --yes` is explicit). `:DevRepositories` and `tv dev-repos` keep native histories/sessions separate. Read `docs/tools/dev-projects.md` before import; the Sidecar config API has no concurrent-writer transaction.
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, binary-matched global skill from `herdr --skill`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with `prefix+d` for the interactive `dev` dashboard, `prefix+G` / `Alt+g` lazygit temporary pane, `prefix+S` for a 50/50 Sidecar pane on the right (Sidecar/td install gate: `installCodingAgents`; exit restores the layout), `prefix+Y` for a Yazi filesystem popup rooted at the focused pane cwd, low-frequency copy helpers under `prefix+y` Quick Actions, `prefix+t` for the interactive `translate` TUI popup, `prefix+y` → *Agent: …* Quick Actions plus `prefix+Alt+c/x/t/r` hotkeys to open claude/codex/opencode/copilot-once agents (SpecStory or direct; right/down split or new tab) via `~/.config/herdr/agent-open.sh` and an rc fast path, and `prefix+y` Quick Actions for bilingual pane translation (current page / last 200-1000 lines; an alternate-screen agent pane has NO scrollback and `pane read` caps at 1000 lines), three metadata pickers (`tv herdr-panes` / `prefix+a` cycles non-shell, agent, process, shell with exact-pane jump, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`), and `herdr-grep` for pane-content search. Yazi itself displays guarded `git.yazi` status signs on Yazi 26.8.15+. See `docs/tools/{herdr,yazi}.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).

`prefix+Alt+e` edits only `$HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` (or `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`), validates that exact live target, and reloads; it never invokes chezmoi. Editor/validation failure preserves the rejected candidate and atomically restores the previous valid config; reload failure keeps the valid edit and backup. A later `chezmoi apply` reasserts canonical `[theme]`, `[ui]`, `[terminal]`, and `[keys]`. Persist selectively by manually editing `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`; never `chezmoi add` or `chezmoi re-add` this `modify_` target.

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~50 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

**"What did this repo install / is X installed here / which role installs it?"** →
`tv inventory` (or read `~/.config/docs/tools/tool-catalog.toml` directly; per-tool
status: `~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py preview <id>`). It marks each tool
installed / missing / gated-off-by-prompt / not-for-this-OS on the current host.

Handy ones: `inventory`, `fleet-hosts`, `tailnet`, `ssh-config`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`,
`kill-process`, `services`, `sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`,
`mac-apps`/`linux-apps`, the agent trio (`agent-panes`, `agent-sessions`,
`agent-wakeup`, dual tmux/Herdr scheduling) and the `herdr-*` family. Full reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

Herdr wakeups prefer stable agent IDs and follow moves; ID-less scheduling pins
a local process fingerprint, refusing unavailable/changed/unverifiable identity.
That fallback cannot follow pane moves or conversation switches in a live process.
Scheduled sends require idle/done except recognized blocked quota Enter menus.
Text uses Herdr `agent prompt` with bounded startup verification; menu Enter uses
`agent send-keys`. A timeout/stall never auto-retries; inspect before resubmitting.
Quota guards use the active tail and are enabled only on detection at scheduling
unless `--no-expect-quota`; `--force` bypasses quota only, not identity/readiness.
One-shot only: host awake, pueued/Herdr/agent running, no reopen or exact timing
guarantee. Shell interface unchanged. Details: `docs/tools/pueue.md` and
`docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` opens the action menu. There is **no `prefix + e`** —
  that alias was removed, and `prefix + E` is "break every pane into its own
  window", so do not guess it. `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools.
  Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- **lazygit** (`lg`): Files `Alt+s` opens repository-wide staged/unstaged/overall line statistics; `/` uses fuzzy filtering, and the focused side panel expands. Local branches `I` opens branch insights. See `docs/tools/lazygit.md`.
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

## SSH layout and machine management

New SSH seeds use grouped directories and explicit Include order with four-space
indentation; existing flat/wildcard layouts stay create-only. Use `dev ssh format`
for indentation preview and opt into `dev ssh organize` for complete Host-block
and comment moves with private recovery. `dev ssh manage` handles explicit
SSH/fleet/Herdr registrations; dotfiles apply never registers machines. The SSH
Television channel prefers dev's static active-alias listing and has a grouped-file
fallback. See `docs/tutorials/setup_ssh_key_on_remote.md` in the source repository.

Herdr UI (`herdr-gpui`) follows `installBrewApps`: macOS cask (14.2+), Ubuntu/Debian desktop verified .deb (glibc 2.39+, x64/ARM64, sudo). Apply installs missing copies only; UI settings stay app-owned. Upgrade via Homebrew / App Updates, separately from `just upgrade-herdr`. See `docs/tools/herdr.md`.

# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

- **External editor** — init default `nvim` (independent of `enableVimMode`); `editorcfg status/list/use/reset/doctor` manages the local override. `EDITOR`/`VISUAL` name `dotfiles-editor`, which resolves and waits on each invocation. Micro is baseline devtools; code/cursor presets add `--wait`. See `docs/tools/editor.md`. Local `editor-choice` is not chezmoi-managed.

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, Pi (`pi`), Oh My Pi (`omp`), the `pia` Git-managed harness-combo manager, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). `pia doctor` checks the stack; `pia list --tree` / `pia use pi/base` select presets. The external checkout is `~/.local/share/pi-agents`; `08_pi_agents.sh` makes its canonical commands beat mise/Bun shadows, while runtime state and credentials stay elsewhere. Token-usage tracking: `tokens` (tokens.ci; binary only — `tokens login` / `tokens serve` are manual opt-ins, see `docs/tools/tokens.md`). See `docs/tools/pi-agents.md`, `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Sidecar + `td` + Tasks** — `coding_agents` installs all three under `installCodingAgents`. Tasks first-seeds user-owned XDG config/data paths; it preserves existing configuration and does not start its API. Herdr `prefix+S` opens a right companion pane, keeping the existing agent external. See `docs/tools/td_sidecar.md` (`#ux-evolution`) and `docs/tools/tasks.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **summarize** — `summarize <url|file>` turns a YouTube video, podcast, webpage, PDF or local media into a summary. Output defaults to 繁體中文 via the managed `~/.summarize/config.json` overlay. Wrappers in `32_summarize.sh`: `ytsum` (video, with timestamps), `sumq` (30-second triage), `suml` (long), `sumj` (JSON). `--cli claude|codex|gemini` reuses an already-authenticated agent instead of an API key. See `docs/tools/summarize.md`.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **mole** (`mo`, macOS only) — `mo purge` reclaims dev build artifacts (`node_modules`, `target`, `.venv`) across the roots listed in `~/.config/mole/purge_paths`; `mo analyze` is a disk explorer, `mo clean` clears caches (always `--dry-run` first, or use the `moclean` wrapper). Helpers in `33_mole.sh`: `moa`, `moclean`, `mowl`. Both config files are chezmoi `create_` seeds, and the whitelist **replaces** rather than extends mole's built-in defaults. See `docs/tools/mole.md`.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared (expose localhost to the **public** internet).
- **Tailscale** — WireGuard mesh VPN (tailnet-only, the opposite of the tunnel tools). Helper CLI: `tsnet`. Picker: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`, `docs/tools/Tailscale.md`.
- **Input method** — McBopomofo + RIME (Traditional Chinese).
- **Agent sounds** — audio notifications on agent Stop/Notification hooks. See `docs/tools/agent-sounds.md`.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Agent browser tools

**Ghostty** is GUI-managed: macOS `installBrewApps` cask; Linux desktop native
apt/PPA with classic Snap fallback (sudo, x64/arm64). Config is shared with
cmux, uses Hack Nerd Font Mono 14, padding 10, native keyboard protocols and SSH
terminfo helpers. Server hosts use a local GUI client over SSH. Details:
`docs/tools/ghostty.md`.

**Agent browser tools** have independent `installTerminalBrowser` (this host: true) and `installPlaywrightCli` (true) switches on supported macOS/Linux hosts, including servers. Use `terminal-browser open URL --split right` for a visible
shared page (Ghostty/Kitty graphics required), and
`playwright-cli -s=TASK open URL --browser=chromium` for independent headless testing. Both have package-matched
skills. Chromium preload/cache repair is opt-in (`preloadPlaywrightChromium`, this host: true). Otherwise first run `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` (Linux missing libraries: add `--with-deps`). Remote preview:
run `terminal-browser open --ssh HOST http://localhost:PORT` **locally**; a remote
agent does not automatically control that local browser. See
`docs/tools/browser-tools.md` for platform/noRoot limits and upgrades. Use the
project's own Playwright Test for committed CI tests.

## Package-managed personal CLIs

`installPersonalTools` groups dev, translate, exp and ten lazy CLIs. Full
bundles default on; cloud-vm/minimal off. Missing keys preserve legacy selection;
choose explicitly with `dotcfg --set installPersonalTools=true --yes --no-apply`.
Apply installs CLIs only (no daemons/credentials or first-use shims). New macOS
binary installs use the personal tap; Linux amd64/arm64 uses verified releases without
Go. `just upgrade-personal` preserves the active owner and skips missing/unknown
binaries; generated Bash/Zsh completions follow successful changes. See
`docs/tools/personal-tools.md`. `gopls` stays in generic `go_tools`.

- **`dev`** — repository/task/worktree command center with a TUI, parent-shell navigation, generated completion, agent-safe prepare/finalize/done/retire lifecycle, and receipt-backed `dev git` transactions. macOS installs `daviddwlee84/tap/dev-cli`; Linux uses the personal release installer (legacy Go remains supported). Source: `github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli`.
- **`translate`** — terminal translator (CLI + TUI). macOS installs `daviddwlee84/tap/translate`; Linux uses the personal release installer (legacy Go remains supported).
- **`lazyclash`** — CLI/TUI for local or SSH-accessible Mihomo cores, source-backed node/group editing and explicit native/Docker client setup. macOS uses the personal tap; Linux new installs use verified releases in `~/.local/bin`, while legacy hosts retain source ownership. Upgrade through `just upgrade-personal` or the owning package manager. The apply-time completion generator owns zsh/bash files; narrow refresh: `scripts/generate_completions.sh --tool lazyclash --force`. v0.1.6+ supplies standalone `proxy shell-init` used by `50_networking.sh`: proxy-on/off own per-shell SSH sessions and restore previous env; set `LAZYCLASH_PROXY_SHELL=0` for legacy helpers. v0.1.7 adds `proxy ssh HOST [-- COMMAND...]` and foreground `proxy tunnel share HOST` for the opposite direction; printed exports belong on the remote host. Copilot startup and `docker-net on` check service lifetime and refuse known temporary SSH endpoints before side effects. Docker render/test generates consumer settings without writing the chezmoi-owned client `proxies.default`; legacy cache consumers reject private proxy credentials. Dotfiles apply installs only the CLI; `lazyclash setup` separately previews and installs a core with its own owner/rollback record. Source: `github.com/daviddwlee84/lazyclash`.

- **`exp`** — Git-based research records, execution and a read-only overview.
- **`lazychezmoi`** — inspect/edit/apply dotfile state through chezmoi.
- **`lazymlflow`** — experiment/run/artifact exploration; local stores may need MLflow separately.
- **`lazypueue`** — task and queue dashboard; Pueue daemons are configured separately.
- **`lazymermaid`** — Mermaid workbench; Neovim/termaid/Node runtime setup remains explicit.
- **`lazyset`** — local/SSH TUI catalog and retained child sessions; underlying tools install independently.
- **`lazyansible`** — personal Ansible workspace fork; existing Ansible runtime stays separately owned.
- **`lazycrontab`** — local/SSH cron inspection, readable schedules and reviewed edits; no scheduler setup during apply.
- **`lazyfind`** — local/SSH file/text search using fd/rg, with optional rga/zoxide.
- **`lazypkg`** — software inventory and reviewed package operations; mpm setup is explicit. Its `upgrade` command updates a selected package, not lazypkg itself; use `lazypkg self upgrade` for verified Homebrew ownership or `just upgrade-personal` for this CLI.

## Copilot agent launchers

`claude-copilot-once` / `codex-copilot-once` (and the identical names without
`-once`) auto-start the local proxy and inject single-session CLI settings.
`--specstory-mode run|exit|off` defaults to live recording; `exit` exports saved
history after the agent exits and retries pending sync next launch. Wrapper
flags precede agent arguments. Claude merges the effective user `--settings`
JSON/file into one CLI object; no temporary project pin. `copilot-here on`
explicitly pins Claude, previews changed settings (default keep; `--yes` for
scripts), and refuses tracked targets. `off` restores owned settings while
preserving later edits. Codex 0.156.1 ignores project-local provider settings;
use its single-session launcher. `copilot-run` remains a generic environment
injector. See `docs/tools/copilot-claude-proxy.md`.

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`. Most have `docs/tools/<name>.md`, but not all (`x` → `clipboard.md`, `view-ebook` → `yazi-previews.md`, `fleet` → `this_repo/fleet-apply.md`); grep `docs/` if the obvious path 404s. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** / **`view-ebook`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) and ebooks (epub/mobi/azw3, calibre-backed) in the terminal; also power the yazi previewers. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`, `docs/tools/yazi-previews.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`tsnet`** — Tailscale helper: `tsnet list` (tailnet devices, `--tsv`/`--json`), `tsnet ssh-config <machine>` (idempotent managed block in `~/.ssh/config.d/20-tailscale`; detects the legacy no-`Include` case and shadowing `Host` blocks, both of which make ssh config silently inert), `tsnet serve <port>` (preflight → `tailscale serve --bg --https=443` → verify, for services that hard-require an `https://` origin), `tsnet doctor`. `--host H` drives any of it on a remote box over ssh. Picker twin: `tv tailnet`. See `docs/tools/tsnet.md`.
- **`agent-warmup`** — Tyro CLI that drives a real interactive Claude TUI at a scheduled time through an existing Herdr session (preferred) or tmux, with uv-first daemon bootstrap and safe fallback. See `docs/tools/agent-warmup.md`.
- **`crash-blackbox`** — flight recorder for hard power-offs / unclean shutdowns. See `docs/tools/crash-blackbox.md`.
- **`nvidia-driver-drift-check`** — flag kernel-module vs userspace driver drift. See `docs/sysadmin/gpu-driver.md`.
- **`raid-perm-check`** — read-only auditor for a group+ACL-shared data mount (`summary`/`orphans`/`groups`/`units`/`user`/`all`, default `/mnt/raid`). Catches the two silent breakages: orphaned uid/gid after an account is deleted, and a stale `systemd --user` manager whose frozen groups make timers hit EACCES on paths your shell reads fine. Never modifies — prints the fix. See `docs/sysadmin/shared-storage-permissions.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`ytmv`** — download YouTube music videos for **old MP3 players**: mp3 + sidecar `.lrc` + ID3v2.3/USLT lyrics, or mp4 with soft/burned-in subtitles. Subcommands `get` / `lyrics` / `tag` / `doctor`; `ytmv help` is the complete setup/cookie-safety guide and `doctor --cookies` explicitly tests a configured source. Public downloads use packaged EJS + managed Node 22+ cookie-free first (doctor flags legacy Node 20/16). Compatibility profiles (`safe`, `cjk-big5`, `cjk-gbk`, `ipod`, `modern`) are re-appliable offline via `ytmv tag`. Needs ffmpeg (`installMediaTools`); `--burn-subs` needs the keg-only `ffmpeg-full`. No `tv` channel by design. See `docs/tools/ytmv.md`.
- **`appsrc`** — detect how an installed app / CLI was installed & managed (cask / App Store / direct-download / apt / snap / flatpak / AppImage / cargo/npm/pipx/uv/mise/go/gem / manual): `appsrc which <cmd-or-app>` (live), `appsrc size <app>` (footprint + associated cache/data/containers), `appsrc tui` (interactive dashboard — sort by size, filter), bare `appsrc` / `appsrc scan` (cached inventory, `--json`/`--tsv`/`--size`/`--sort`). Picker twins: `tv appsrc` (by source) / `tv appsrc-size` (by footprint). See `docs/tools/appsrc.md`.
- **`herdr-grep`** — search visible or retained content across panes in the current, one named, or all running local Herdr sessions; reports exact session/workspace/tab/pane coordinates, supports `--json`, and `--pick` pipes matches to fzf then exact-focuses/attaches the selection. Inside Herdr, `prefix+Alt+F` opens a visible-content picker (Alt+S = scrollback, Alt+V = visible). Remote use runs the CLI through SSH. See `docs/tools/herdr.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`dev-projects`** — on-demand local REPOS candidates from `dev repo list --json`; `open PATH --tool sidecar|nvim` revalidates before launch, and `sidecar-import` previews add-only registration (`--apply --yes` is explicit). `:DevRepositories` and `tv dev-repos` keep native histories/sessions separate. Read `docs/tools/dev-projects.md` before import; the Sidecar config API has no concurrent-writer transaction.
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

**`herdr`** is a first-class managed surface too (config in `dot_config/herdr/`, binary-matched global skill from `herdr --skill`, upgrade via `just upgrade-herdr` — which must NOT be run from inside a herdr pane): a remote pane/workspace server with `prefix+d` for the interactive `dev` dashboard, `prefix+G` / `Alt+g` lazygit temporary pane, `prefix+S` for a 50/50 Sidecar pane on the right (Sidecar/td install gate: `installCodingAgents`; exit restores the layout), `prefix+Y` for a Yazi filesystem popup rooted at the focused pane cwd, low-frequency copy helpers under `prefix+y` Quick Actions, `prefix+t` for the interactive `translate` TUI popup, `prefix+y` → *Agent: …* Quick Actions plus `prefix+Alt+c/x/t/r` hotkeys to open claude/codex/opencode/copilot-once agents (SpecStory or direct; right/down split or new tab) via `~/.config/herdr/agent-open.sh` and an rc fast path, and `prefix+y` Quick Actions for bilingual pane translation (current page / last 200-1000 lines; an alternate-screen agent pane has NO scrollback and `pane read` caps at 1000 lines), three metadata pickers (`tv herdr-panes` / `prefix+a` cycles non-shell, agent, process, shell with exact-pane jump, `tv herdr-review`, `tv herdr-sesh`), and `herdr-grep` for pane-content search. Yazi itself displays guarded `git.yazi` status signs on Yazi 26.8.15+. See `docs/tools/{herdr,yazi}.md` and the herdr entries in `pitfalls/`. Distinct from `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux).

`prefix+Alt+e` edits only `$HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` (or `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`), validates that exact live target, and reloads; it never invokes chezmoi. Editor/validation failure preserves the rejected candidate and atomically restores the previous valid config; reload failure keeps the valid edit and backup. A later `chezmoi apply` reasserts canonical `[theme]`, `[ui]`, `[terminal]`, and `[keys]`. Persist selectively by manually editing `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`; never `chezmoi add` or `chezmoi re-add` this `modify_` target.

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~50 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

**"What did this repo install / is X installed here / which role installs it?"** →
`tv inventory` (or read `~/.config/docs/tools/tool-catalog.toml` directly; per-tool
status: `~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py preview <id>`). It marks each tool
installed / missing / gated-off-by-prompt / not-for-this-OS on the current host.

Handy ones: `inventory`, `fleet-hosts`, `tailnet`, `ssh-config`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`,
`kill-process`, `services`, `sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`,
`mac-apps`/`linux-apps`, the agent trio (`agent-panes`, `agent-sessions`,
`agent-wakeup`, dual tmux/Herdr scheduling) and the `herdr-*` family. Full reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

Herdr wakeups prefer stable agent IDs and follow moves; ID-less scheduling pins
a local process fingerprint, refusing unavailable/changed/unverifiable identity.
That fallback cannot follow pane moves or conversation switches in a live process.
Scheduled sends require idle/done except recognized blocked quota Enter menus.
Text uses Herdr `agent prompt` with bounded startup verification; menu Enter uses
`agent send-keys`. A timeout/stall never auto-retries; inspect before resubmitting.
Quota guards use the active tail and are enabled only on detection at scheduling
unless `--no-expect-quota`; `--force` bypasses quota only, not identity/readiness.
One-shot only: host awake, pueued/Herdr/agent running, no reopen or exact timing
guarantee. Shell interface unchanged. Details: `docs/tools/pueue.md` and
`docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` opens the action menu. There is **no `prefix + e`** —
  that alias was removed, and `prefix + E` is "break every pane into its own
  window", so do not guess it. `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools.
  Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- **lazygit** (`lg`): Files `Alt+s` opens repository-wide staged/unstaged/overall line statistics; `/` uses fuzzy filtering, and the focused side panel expands. Local branches `I` opens branch insights. See `docs/tools/lazygit.md`.
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

## SSH layout and machine management

New SSH seeds use grouped directories and explicit Include order with four-space
indentation; existing flat/wildcard layouts stay create-only. Use `dev ssh format`
for indentation preview and opt into `dev ssh organize` for complete Host-block
and comment moves with private recovery. `dev ssh manage` handles explicit
SSH/fleet/Herdr registrations; dotfiles apply never registers machines. The SSH
Television channel prefers dev's static active-alias listing and has a grouped-file
fallback. See `docs/tutorials/setup_ssh_key_on_remote.md` in the source repository.

Herdr UI (`herdr-gpui`) follows `installBrewApps`: macOS cask (14.2+), Ubuntu/Debian desktop verified .deb (glibc 2.39+, x64/ARM64, sudo). Apply installs missing copies only; UI settings stay app-owned. Upgrade via Homebrew / App Updates, separately from `just upgrade-herdr`. See `docs/tools/herdr.md`.

52	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
53	
54	The `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism spans **6 surfaces that must move together** — devtools install, `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml`, `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`, `dot_claude/modify_settings.json.tmpl` hooks, `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` (+ its `modify_package.json`), and `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh`'s producers API. Exact contents: [workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md) § Status icon mechanics; why it leaks: [workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md).
55	
56	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (writes parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears). The workmux hook entries are **unconditional** — the `agentSounds` prompt gates only the notify.sh / peon-ping entries in the same file. `wt` (worktrunk) and `wm` (workmux) stay distinct tools.
57

59	
60	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` agent skill (restored on every `chezmoi apply`; see [agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md)). **Load the skill** for the template and disambiguation table.

62	**Fallback rules**, so this still binds when the skill can't be loaded:
63	
64	- Three repo-root surfaces, all chezmoi-ignored, all NOT auto-redacted: [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) (tags `P1`/`P2`/`P3`/`P?` × `S`/`M`/`L`/`XL`), [`backlog/`](backlog/README.md) (notes for `P?` / `[L]` / `[XL]` / multi-option), [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/README.md) (debugged traps — **title by symptom, not root cause**, verbatim error messages, never paraphrase).
65	- Capture triggers — future work: "maybe later", "nice to have", "工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來". Pitfalls: >~15 min debugging, not googleable, non-obvious fix, silent failure.
66	- Do **not** spawn `ROADMAP.md` / `IDEAS.md` / `LESSONS.md` / `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`. Three surfaces, always.
67	- A pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant below when it recurs across machines, silently corrupts state, or has a non-obvious workaround. Link back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md`.

69	## Chezmoi templating conventions
70	
71	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask whether the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` (`darwin`/`linux`) / `.chezmoi.arch` (`arm64`/`amd64`) / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for **user-role choices only**, and its values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts. `.profile` is still the right knob for desktop-vs-headless.
72	
73	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
74	
75	Predicate table, examples, the `macos_intel` migration: [chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
76	
77	## Hard repo invariants
78	
79	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
80	
81	YAML / TOML / JSON syntax and template rendering are not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (`codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is only a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
82	
83	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
84	
85	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
86	
87	**Hard rules**:
88	
89	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
90	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
91	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
92	
93	The ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be last before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions`/`syntax-highlighting`/`history-substring-search` MUST be excluded (double-init flicker). [bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
94	
95	### Three-tier user-local override layer
96	
97	User overrides live in **six** untracked files, all in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). Default target: shared; drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
98	
99	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl` — `managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc`. Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
100	
101	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
102	
103	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
104	
105	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templates + 2 first-seed files: [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
106	
107	**Hard rules**:
108	
109	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
110	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/`, `dot_config/opencode/`, `dot_cursor/`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
111	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
112	- The `minimal` bundle forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without an explicit request.
113	- New vim-touched file → follow the gate-it-or-not flow in [vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md) → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table there.
114	
115	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
116	
117	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
118	
119	**Hard rules**:
120	
121	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
122	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
123	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a *single* tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it genuinely needs a newer one (`python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5`). It MUST detect the install style and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (silent no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors when it isn't a formula). The dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and the role. See [uv-bootstrap](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
124	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`, or the install guard short-circuits and entry-point shims are never written (silently missing `jupyter` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit command: [uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
125	- New upgrade category: [upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) § Adding a new category. Tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise → do nothing, generic `upgrade` picks it up.
126	- **Probe `brew` by output, never exit status** — `[[ -n "$(brew --prefix 2>/dev/null)" ]]`. A stub `brew` passes `command -v brew` and returns 0 with empty output for *every* subcommand: `brew bundle` silently installs nothing and `community.general.homebrew` dies on `Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`. [ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md](pitfalls/ansible-homebrew-expecting-value-line-1-column-1.md)
127	
128	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
129	
130	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
131	
132	**Hard rules**:
133	
134	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
135	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
136	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
137	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
138	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
139	
140	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**: `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top → set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag → `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"` and branch on its return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason` → run privileged commands via `sudo_run …` (or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible).
141	
142	For **non-interactive** injection (`scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH), `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (0600) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty` — **never** read that variable directly, always go through the helper. Full API + state + cleanup model: [sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
143	
144	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
145	
146	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
147	
148	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked; hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let the template win.
149	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (`chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`), so ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for those.
150	- **`--branch BRANCH` is a no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS your editor working tree): they warn and run against the working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
151	- **Install-only by design.** `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
152	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
153	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint; anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without an explicit request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
154	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse. `just fleet-status` is the **pre-flight readiness probe** (13 states; always exits 0 — use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates; `fleet-status-quick` skips the remote `git fetch`). `just fleet-apply-status` is a **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`, run during/after, pairing with `fleet-apply-tail`/`-watch`/`-kill`. State meanings incl. `toml-mismatch`: [fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md).
155	- **`fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving** (auto-seed / exit 0 with a hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
156	
157	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
158	
159	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes the current target contents to stdin and expects the new contents on stdout. Used wherever a *foreign writer* also owns part of the file — `~/.claude/settings.json`, editor `settings.json`, the agent CLI configs, `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`, `~/.gitconfig` (preserves the `[credential]` blocks `gh auth setup-git` injects). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it overwrites the script with the live file.
160	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches the contents after (`~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json`, editor `keybindings.json`). Refresh the baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"` — `chezmoi add` strips the prefix and `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
161	
162	Per-file case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). The three agent CLI overlays, incl. the Claude hook merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland) without ping-ponging: [agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
163	
164	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
165	
166	The popup menu (`prefix + Space` / `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two tmux quirks force that: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) instead of clamped — the `devtools` role auto-upgrades Debian/Ubuntu past it — and `display-menu` does **not** paginate, so a menu taller than the terminal is suppressed entirely, with no error anywhere.
167	
168	**Hard rules**:
169	
170	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
171	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
172	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
173	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
174	
175	Full story incl. the red herrings: `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md`, `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
176	
177	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
178	
179	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
180	
181	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps. **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
182	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
183	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
184	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
185	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
186	
187	Full breakdown / themes / keybindings / troubleshooting: [](docs/tools/tmux/).
188	
189	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
190	
191	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` sets `default_mode "locked"` on purpose — all keys pass through to inner apps, `Ctrl+G` unlocks Zellij's own. Do **not** change it. Fresh box → pick the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" preset. [keyboard-shortcuts.md](docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md)
192	
193	### SSH grouped seeds remain create-only
194	
195	New SSH dispatchers explicitly include grouped files; existing flat/wildcard
196	configs must never acquire new active definitions during apply. Keep the grouped
197	seed marker gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` aligned with `private_dot_ssh/` and
198	test fresh and existing destinations. The source dir is `private_dot_ssh` (not
199	`dot_ssh`) so chezmoi owns `~/.ssh` at mode 0700 — matching ssh/`dev ssh` — instead
200	of applying 0755 and drifting forever (see
201	`pitfalls/chezmoi-ssh-dir-mode-drift-prompt.md`). Four spaces is the seed
202	convention; Include order is semantic authority. The shared setup helper uses
203	exact-file Include insertion,
204	and the Television channel prefers dev's active static inventory with a grouped
205	fallback. Config migration is an explicit `dev ssh organize` action, not apply.
